Date: 2024-10-23
REMARKS
I. Overview
Claims 1-20 are pending in the present application. Claims 8-12 have been amended herein, no claims have been canceled, claims 1-7, and 16-20 have been withdrawn, and no new claims have been added. No new matter has been introduced as a result of these amendments. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the claims in view of the following amendments and remarks.
The issues raised by the Examiner in the current Office Action dated August 1, 2024 ("the Office Action") are as follows:
" The drawings stand objected to as failing to comply with 37 CFR § 1.84(p)(5);
" Corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR § 1.121(d) are required;
" The abstract of the disclosure stands objected to;
" Claims 8 and 9 are not in compliance with MPEP § 608.01(m);
" Claims 8-15 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre- AIA), first paragraph, as failing to comply with the written description
requirement.; and
" Claims 8-15 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre- AIA), first paragraph, as failing to comply with the enablement requirement.
Applicant respectfully traverses the outstanding claim rejections and requests reconsideration and withdrawal in light of the amendments and remarks presented herein.
II. Response to Restriction Requirement
Applicant acknowledges that the Office Action restricted the claims of the present invention to either of Group I (claims 1-7), which are drawn to a shaped aircraft fuel cell comprising a through a void or an edge cavity, Group II (claims 8-15), which are drawn to an aircraft comprising an aircraft structure that translates and a shaped fuel cell comprising a through a void and/or an edge cavity, or Group III (claims 16-20), which are drawn to a method of preventing rupture of fuel cells in an aircraft during a drop impact of the aircraft, wherein a shaped fuel cell comprising one or more through voids and/or one or more edge cavities is provided and installed in an aircraft. Applicant further acknowledges that in response to the restriction requirement, Applicant has elected Group I (claims 8-15) for further prosecution in the above-referenced application.
III. Drawings
The Office Action objected to the drawings under 37 CFR § 1.84(p)(5) because they do not include the following reference sign(s) mentioned in the description, namely 106, central pylon; and 306, frame structure. Applicant has amended the drawings as shown in the enclosed Replacement Sheets 1/6 and 3/6 such that the aforementioned reference numerals are shown in the drawings. Additionally, the Office Action objected to the drawings under 37 CFR §
1.84(p)(5) because they include the following reference character(s) not mentioned in the description, namely 604 and 606 in Fig. 6. Applicant has amended the drawings as shown above such that the aforementioned reference numerals are shown in the Specification. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the objection to the drawings under 37 CFR § 1.84(p)(5) be withdrawn.
IV. Specification
The Office Action objected to the Specification because the Abstract presently contains a plurality of alternative phrasings in parentheses. (Office Action, page 4). Applicant has amended the Abstract as shown above such that the alternative phrasings have been removed. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the objection to the Specification be withdrawn.
V. Claim objections
The Office Action objected to claims(s) 8 and 9 as allegedly not being in compliance with MPEP 608.01(m) which states: "Where a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element or step of the claim should be separated by a line indentation." (Office Action, page 5). Applicant has amended the claims as shown above such that they are now in compliance with MPEP 608.01(m). Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the objection to claims 8 and 9 be withdrawn.
VI. Rejection of claims under 35 U.S.C. § 112
The Office Action rejected claims 8-15 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre- AIA), first paragraph, as failing to comply with the written description requirement. (Office Action, page 6). In particular, the Office Action asserts that there does not appear to be a single aircraft structure which translates into the area and corresponds to both a through-void and an edge cavity as allowed by the phrase "and/or." Applicant has amended claims 8 and 9 such that the aforementioned phrase has been removed.
The Office Action also rejected claims 8-15 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), first paragraph, as failing to comply with the enablement requirement. (Office
Action, page 7). In formulating this rejection, the Office Action asserts that it is presently unclear how the fuel cells would be constructed and/or modified to provide at least a through- void since it's unclear how the internals of a typical stacked anode, cathode, and membrane of a known fuel cell would need to be modified to provide a through-void. (Id, page 8). Applicant respectfully submits that the fuel cell recited in the claims is not a battery having any anode or cathode; rather, the Specification explicitly teaches that the fuel cell is adapted to contain liquid fuel that is used to power one or more engines that drive rotor system and anti-torque system. (Specification, paragraph [0022]).
The Office Action also asserts that it is also unclear how the through-voids and/or edge cavities would have to be sized and shaped to accommodate an aircraft structure translating into the fuel cell area during an impact such as a crash, and what modifications, if any, would be required to the aircraft structures to ensure that they enter the through-void and/or edge cavity in the event of a crash. (Id). Applicant respectfully submits that the Specification as filed explicitly teaches that the through-voids and/or edge cavities would be sized and shaped to accommodate aircraft structures that translate into an area of the fuel cell during a drop impact. (Specification, paragraph [0033]). The Office Action further asserts that the through-void and/or edge cavity have to be sized and shaped to accommodate all possible failure modes of the aircraft structure entering the fuel cell area. (Office Action, page 8). Applicant respectfully submits, however, that with apparatus claims, novelty exists in its structure and not whether it would accommodate some, most, or all failure modes. Apparatus claims cover what a device is, not what a device does." Hewlett-Packard Co. v. Bausch & Lomb Inc., 909 F.2d 1464, 1469, 15 USPQ2d 1525, 1528 (Fed. Cir. 1990).
Given the facts presented above, it is respectfully submitted that claims 8-15 satisfy the description requirement and enablement requirement, and respectfully requests that the § rejections of record be withdrawn.
VII. Conclusion
Applicant has made a diligent effort to place the claims in condition for allowance.
However, should there remain unresolved issues that require adverse action, Applicant requests that the Examiner telephone Applicant's attorney at 214-272-2211 so that such issues may be resolved as expeditiously as possible.
Respectfully submitted,
October 23, 2024 /Gerard E. Moy/
